topics.flagship-ru-ua: U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff briefed Vladimir Putin in the Kremlin after Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, and were due to fly on to Ireland to meet Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Zelensky warned the EU to watch for Russian efforts to rewrite Europe's security architecture before any ceasefire, and reportedly said Starshield satellite communications disruptions are affecting the front line. Other items: the UK took a U.S. service member into custody over alleged leaks to Moscow, the UK sanctioned Russia's top ten oil producers, and the EU is set to add Wildberries CEO Tatyana Kim to its sanctions list.
topics.flagship-ir-il: An Israeli strike on the surgery department of Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis killed at least six and wounded at least 20, according to Gaza's civil defence agency (8 outlets). Separately, Trump and Netanyahu reportedly clashed in a heated phone call over the Iran war, with Trump favouring diplomacy and Netanyahu pressing for military action and regime change. Trump said no Iran deal is needed ('we've got their Strait'), which pushed oil prices up. A London court convicted two Iranian men of spying on journalists, aid groups urged Israel to allow shelters in Gaza after flooding, and the USA withdrew from the U17 World Cup in Qatar over conflict risk.
topics.T15: Coverage is sparse and unrelated. The one concrete item is an evacuation alert, with one section under an evacuation order, for Pemberton (reportedly in British Columbia) over high river flows and heavy rain. The other items are a general piece on El Niño health warnings and an airline route-scheduling note.
topics.T01: Items are scattered, mostly single-source, and do not form one narrative. A drone strike in Sudan's Blue Nile state reportedly killed nine civilians, with a local official blaming the RSF, and displaced families in Tigray fear renewed fighting. Reuters reportedly raised questions about a Trump donor's Venezuela oil deal after U.S. forces captured someone in Venezuela. The rest is opinion and analysis on undersea cables, a possible China war and drone security at Mar-a-Lago.
topics.T02: Coverage is thin and mostly Nigerian. Items include NEMA flood relief in Kogi State and a federal mobile ID registration drive for 3.7 million displaced persons in 10 states. American Airlines resumed daily flights to northern Haiti, and flooding rainstorms are worsening conditions in Gaza.
topics.T04: Kenya refused to act as an Ebola quarantine centre for foreign travelers (4 outlets), though the excerpt gives no further detail. A contagious disease outbreak linked to close contact and contaminated bedding has closed some UK hospital wards, and Knox County declared a measles public health emergency despite having no active cases. The remaining items are academic papers.
topics.T05: Stories are sparse and generic. Japan's PM Takaichi is set to attend APEC in her first China trip amid fraught relations, and a commentary discusses how to make Ethiopia's peace agreement enforceable. No coup or instability event is reported.
topics.T06: Spain's first general strike in 14 years turned violent in Barcelona, where protesters set fires and launched fireworks at riot police on Paseo de Gracia (3 outlets). Spain's parliament later passed housing reforms limiting evictions. Other items are partisan or opinion-driven, including claims of migrant-linked riots in Europe, French polling on riots, and Omoyele Sowore's call for a revolution against Nigeria's President Tinubu.
topics.T08: A militant attack in Kohat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, killed at least 10 police, including two senior officers, and a gunbattle was still under way (3 outlets). Indian security agencies are hunting LeT-affiliated militant Mohammad Lateef Bhat after an attack on CRPF personnel in Kulgam, and a woman was reportedly shot dead in a suspected militant attack in Manipur. In Europe, over 1,800 Italian schools received hoax bomb alerts amid hybrid-warfare concerns, and a bomb alert at Calais-Fréthun station delayed Eurostar services.
topics.T09: The only item is a retrospective on Evan Gershkovich's 2023 FSB arrest and later release in a prisoner swap. It reports no new hostage or kidnapping case.
topics.T10: Indian military leaders are pushing for fully indigenous drones and dedicated cyber and space doctrines. U.S. scrutiny of China's access to AI chips is growing: a PLA-linked university reportedly bought Nvidia H200 chips despite a blacklist (3 outlets), and a scandal involving Jensen Huang is fueling calls for tighter curbs ahead of a Trump-Xi summit. Other items cover Poland's arms buildup, autonomous weapons for smaller NATO militaries, a critical commentary on Hegseth and a Swedish caretaker budget.
topics.T11: The 8th India–Myanmar Naval Exercise (IMNEX-26) began at Visakhapatnam and runs Nov 10–14, 2026. Myanmar's UMS King Sin Phyu Shin is taking part alongside INS Rana and INS Sumedha (6 outlets).
topics.T12: Poland temporarily took its ePUAP e-government platform offline after detecting and stopping a cyberattack, disrupting public services. Romania's intelligence agency identified a Russian-linked cyberattack, Maersk confirmed a data breach with a $5 million ransom demand (reported), and Europol seized servers and domains tied to Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC. Other items include a Reuters poll finding a third of Japanese firms hit this year, a UK public preparedness drive that boosted sales of sanitiser, water and batteries, and a report on Qilin ransomware's administrator.
topics.T13: Trump reportedly threatened to double tariffs on Mexico if it does not stop migrant caravans heading to the U.S. border. The other items are single-source and unrelated: Ethiopian refugee mothers in Kenya, UK asylum housing contractors, Syrian asylum seekers in London, and an unsourced claim of record Canary Islands arrivals.
topics.T14: A report with no independent corroboration says the U.S. Embassy in Riyadh issued a security alert over Houthi attack threats and ordered non-emergency staff and their families to leave Saudi Arabia. This is unverified and should be confirmed with official sources.
topics.T16: Spain's parliament passed housing reforms limiting evictions, but their duration depends on the outcome of an upcoming snap election (2 outlets). In the U.S., Democrats reportedly secured at least 54 Senate seats and gained in the House, with Mississippi and Alaska races still being counted. Other items include Likud preparing an appeal over polling-station results in Arab communities, Nigerian 2027 election positioning (Makinde challenging Tinubu), and Cabo Verde's presidential election.
